SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Breathing difficulty approximately 15 minutes after a wasp sting sustained while gardening.
- History of presenting illness:
  • Symptoms: shallow breathing, chest tightness, tingling sensation in lips (no throat swelling reported), blotchy rash on body.  
  • First occurrence; no prior similar reactions.
- Past medical history: eczema.
- Medications: keeps over-the-counter antihistamines for airsickness/aerosinusitis (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: penicillin.
- Social history: wife present at home; no additional details provided.

Objective:
- Telemedicine visit; no direct physical examination or vitals obtained.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Suspected anaphylactic reaction to wasp sting
   - Assessment: Likely evolving anaphylaxis given respiratory symptoms (shallow breathing, chest tightness), oral tingling, and cutaneous rash soon after sting.
   - Differential: Local allergic reaction with anxiety; systemic toxic reaction (less likely).
   - Treatment/management:
     • Instructed patient to take available oral antihistamine immediately.
     • Advised immediate activation of emergency medical services (EMS) for transport to Emergency Department; ambulance recommended rather than private conveyance.
   - Follow-up: Emergency care urgency emphasized; no routine follow-up set during call.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements:
  – Vital signs, peak flow/oxygen saturation, full medication list, and comprehensive social history were not obtainable via teleconsult.  
  – No documentation of prior tetanus status, prior stings, or epinephrine autoinjector availability.

• Internal conflicts: none noted.

• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; occasional minor pauses but clinical content understandable.
